logicalBugs.explanation: A model is a saved, table-like query that other questions can use as a data source; it can also have custom column labels, types and display settings. Open the Actions page for a model saved in a personal collection; actions are forms that run SQL against that model’s database. Its location breadcrumb says “Our analytics” instead of the personal collection containing the model, although the model itself was not moved.

rootCause.explanation: ModelActions uses a separate loaded model container from the query builder; the navigation breadcrumb falls back to root collection context instead of using the loaded model collection.

reproductionPaths.explanation: A model is a reusable saved query displayed as a table or list, with configurable column labels and formatting. Open the Actions page for a model saved in a personal collection; actions are forms that run SQL against that model’s database. Its location breadcrumb says “Our analytics” instead of the personal collection containing the model, although the model itself was not moved.

sourceBugs.name: Personal model Actions view shows the wrong collection

reproductionPaths.expected: A personal model’s breadcrumb should show its actual collection.
reproductionPaths.actual: The Actions view of a model in a personal collection shows “Our analytics” in the breadcrumb instead of the model’s collection.
reproSteps: Save a model in your personal collection.
Open the model’s Actions view.
Compare the breadcrumb with the model’s saved collection.

logicalBugs.explanation: Data Reference is a catalog of database tables and columns, with descriptions, related records and suggested questions for exploring their data. The supplied Orders table’s ID description calls it a product identifier even though Orders has its own row ID and a separate Product ID. The reference text describes the wrong kind of record; the stored IDs need not be incorrect.

rootCause.explanation: The sample-data field record contains an incorrect description, consumed directly by the reference/metadata UI. The upstream frontend cannot establish the original seeded record or authoring location.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Data Reference is a catalog of database tables and columns, with descriptions, related records and suggested questions for exploring their data. The supplied Orders table’s ID description calls it a product identifier even though Orders has its own row ID and a separate Product ID. The reference text describes the wrong kind of record; the stored IDs need not be incorrect.

sourceBugs.name: Orders ID metadata describes a product identifier

reproductionPaths.expected: Orders ID metadata should describe an order identifier.
reproductionPaths.actual: The Orders table ID field description calls it a unique product ID although Orders also has a distinct Product ID field.
reproSteps: Open Sample Database > Orders and inspect field metadata.
Compare the descriptions of ID and Product ID.

logicalBugs.explanation: Questions are saved queries, models are reusable table-like queries and metrics are saved aggregate calculations. Each has a title, a collection location and revision history. Opening History on a dashboard, model or metric can show “undefined modified this” where the person’s name should be. The observable failure is the literal missing-name text in an existing revision entry, not the absence of history or a claim that an unauthorized actor edited the item.

rootCause.explanation: Timeline revision copy reads r.user.common_name directly for another actor, without reconstructing a name or providing a fallback when the seeded revision user lacks that property.

sourceBugs.name: Metric history displays an undefined actor

reproductionPaths.explanation: A metric is a saved calculation such as a count or average. Open History on a supplied metric: an existing revision says “undefined modified this” instead of naming its author or using a neutral fallback.
reproductionPaths.expected: Metric history should show an actor name or a neutral fallback.
reproductionPaths.actual: The History tab contains the entry undefined modified this.
reproSteps: Open Data > Metrics > Number of Orders and select Start exploring if prompted.
Open More info > History.
Read the actor name in the history entry.

sourceBugs.name: Seeded model History displays “undefined modified this.”

reproductionPaths.explanation: A model is a reusable saved query presented as a table or list. Open History on a supplied model: an existing revision says “undefined modified this” instead of identifying who made the change. This is missing author text, not missing revision history.
reproductionPaths.expected: A history entry should show a meaningful actor name or neutral fallback.
reproductionPaths.actual: The visible history entry reads “undefined modified this.”
reproSteps: Open Orders + People from Models.
Open More info and select History.

logicalBugs.explanation: The embedding wizard configures how a saved question or dashboard is displayed outside Metabase, including a live preview and initial or locked filter values. With German selected, the metric-embedding setup sentence leaves the English word “question” or its untranslated substitution in the displayed text. The language error is in the setup explanation, not a failed embed or a changed metric type.

rootCause.explanation: The German translation for the embed question/type interpolation does not substitute the intended resource label. The relevant locale string is not proved by the component alone.

reproductionPaths.explanation: A metric is a saved calculation that can be embedded outside Metabase. Set the interface language to German and open metric embedding setup. The parameter guidance retains the English word “question” in “Dieses question hat noch keine konfigurierbaren Parameter” rather than translating the item description.

sourceBugs.name: German metric embed copy contains an untranslated question token

reproductionPaths.expected: The German parameter guidance should use a German term for question.
reproductionPaths.actual: The embed panel says “Dieses question hat noch keine konfigurierbaren Parameter.”
reproSteps: Set the Metabase account language to German.
Open Browse metrics > Number of Orders and choose Teilen > Einbetten.
Read the guidance under Parameter.

logicalBugs.explanation: A model created from an uploaded CSV file can receive more rows by append or replace all of its existing uploaded rows with another file. A successful CSV append or replacement produces a notification whose filename link opens a blank new question instead of the updated model. The upload itself succeeds; the broken destination is the link in its success message.

rootCause.explanation: The upload notification constructs a model link from the upload result while append/replace responses do not supply the same model identifier as new-model creation.

reproductionPaths.explanation: An uploaded-CSV model is a saved table-like view of the uploaded data. Successfully append or replace its rows, then click the filename link in the success notification. It leads to /model/undefined and a blank New question rather than the updated model; the upload itself succeeded.

sourceBugs.name: CSV append and replacement notifications link to /model/undefined

reproductionPaths.expected: The success notification's filename link opens the existing model receiving the uploaded data.
reproductionPaths.actual: Both append and replace notifications link to /model/undefined. Clicking redirects to a blank New question with no starting data, although row changes persist.
reproSteps: Sign in as administrator. In Admin settings → Uploads, enable uploads using Sample Database and PUBLIC schema.
Open a personal collection and upload AD Upload.csv with columns name,amount,date and rows Alpha,10,2026-10-01; Beta,20,2026-10-02; Gamma,30,2026-10-03.
Open the created Ad Upload model.
Choose Upload data to this model → Append data to this model and upload AD Append.csv with the same columns and row Delta,40,2026-10-04.
Click AD Append.csv in the successful 'Data added to' notification. The link targets /model/undefined and opens an empty new question.
Alternatively, use Upload data to this model → Replace all data in this model with another CSV of the same columns. Its successful 'Data replaced in' notification has the same broken filename link.

logicalBugs.explanation: A metric is a saved, reusable aggregate such as a count or average; its definition chooses source data, filters, formula and an optional date grouping for showing changes over time. Attempt to save a new metric before selecting its starting data. The failure exposes a raw DATABASE_ID database constraint and SQL INSERT text instead of identifying the missing source in the editor.

rootCause.explanation: MetricEditorHeader disables Save changes for saved metrics using !isRunnable||!isDirty, but its new-metric Save button has no disabled/isRunnable condition. It therefore opens creation/save for an incomplete metric with no database/source.

reproductionPaths.explanation: A metric is a saved calculation such as a count or average, optionally grouped by a date. Attempt to save a new metric before selecting its starting data. The failure exposes a raw DATABASE_ID database constraint and SQL INSERT text instead of identifying the missing source in the editor.

sourceBugs.name: Saving a metric without a data source exposes a raw DATABASE_ID SQL error

reproductionPaths.expected: Explain that starting data must be selected and tell the user how to correct the metric, rather than exposing a database exception and SQL statement.
reproductionPaths.actual: Saving with the Data picker empty displays NULL not allowed for column "DATABASE_ID" and the SQL INSERT statement. The raw error remains after the Failed button returns to Save.
reproSteps: Sign in as a user who can create metrics and open /browse/metrics.
Create a new metric with the plus button and leave the Data picker empty.
Click Save, enter a fresh unique name, and choose a collection where the user can save metrics.
Submit the save dialog and observe the DATABASE_ID constraint error and SQL INSERT statement instead of guidance to select starting data.

logicalBugs.explanation: A model created from an uploaded CSV file can receive more rows by append or replace all of its existing uploaded rows with another file. Replace an already populated uploaded model with a CSV containing an invalid number or date. Validation reports failure, but the old rows have already been deleted instead of being preserved when the replacement cannot complete; this differs from a successful replacement intentionally removing previous rows.

rootCause.explanation: update-with-csv! calls driver/truncate! before driver/insert-into! in a try/catch without a transaction/rollback, so an insert failure leaves the original rows already deleted.

reproductionPaths.explanation: A model is a reusable saved query. An uploaded-CSV model already contains saved rows. Choose Replace with a file containing an invalid number or date: the upload reports a parsing error, but reopening the model shows no rows because its earlier data was deleted. This is failure to preserve data after a rejected replacement, not the intended removal during a successful replacement.

sourceBugs.name: Failed CSV replacement deletes existing model data

reproductionPaths.expected: An invalid replacement is rejected and leaves the existing model data unchanged.
reproductionPaths.actual: The upload reports "'notanumber' is not a recognizable number" (or an invalid-date parsing error). After reloading, the model shows 'No results!' and 0 rows; its original data is lost.
reproSteps: As administrator, enable uploads in Admin settings → Uploads using Sample Database and PUBLIC schema.
Upload AD Upload.csv in a collection with columns name,amount,date and rows Alpha,10,2026-10-01; Beta,20,2026-10-02; Gamma,30,2026-10-03.
Open the created model and verify its existing rows.
Choose Upload data to this model → Replace all data in this model. Upload AD Invalid Replacement.csv with the same columns and row Invalid,notanumber,2026-10-08.
Observe the Upload error and numeric parsing error. Close the dialog and reload the model.
Observe 'No results!' and 'Showing 0 rows', rather than the original rows. A replacement containing a valid row followed by an invalid date also produces the same data loss.

logicalBugs.explanation: Data Reference is a catalog of database tables and columns, with descriptions, related records and suggested questions for exploring their data. Open a column’s Data Reference page and click the parent table name in its breadcrumb. The visible table link does not navigate to the table reference, leaving the user on the field page.

rootCause.explanation: Reference header breadcrumb uses retained route/detail state when linking the parent table, so the Accounts parent link fails to reset the active field detail.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Data Reference is a catalog of database tables and columns, with descriptions, related records and suggested questions for exploring their data. Open a column’s Data Reference page and click the parent table name in its breadcrumb. The visible table link does not navigate to the table reference, leaving the user on the field page.

reproSteps: At a 390×844 CSS-pixel viewport, start signed in to the Harbor account using the provided authorized session; no credentials or authentication details were changed. Open the app.
Open the main menu, choose Databases, then Learn about our data, open Sample Database, and select Tables.
Open Accounts, select Fields in the sidebar, and open the ID field details.
Click the visible ACCOUNTS breadcrumb above the ID details. Re-observe the page, click the same breadcrumb again, and wait six seconds.

logicalBugs.explanation: A metric is a saved, reusable aggregate such as a count or average; its definition chooses source data, filters, formula and an optional date grouping for showing changes over time. At tablet widths, the metric viewer wraps its title and collection breadcrumb to roughly one character per line. The header becomes unreadable and pushes its toolbar out of place instead of fitting a usable title/navigation layout.

rootCause.explanation: The metric header and collection navigation share a constrained flex row without sufficient minimum-width/shrink handling; long labels wrap to individual characters.

The header becomes unreadable and pushes its toolbar out of place instead of fitting a usable title/navigation layout.

reproductionPaths.expected: The selected metric's title and breadcrumb should remain readable, with the viewer toolbar in a usable layout at 820×1180 CSS pixels.
reproductionPaths.actual: At 820×1180, the “Examples” breadcrumb and “Number of Orders” title are each rendered in a very narrow vertical strip, with one character per line. The toolbar appears much lower in the content area beside the strip, even though the chart occupies the broader viewer area.

Clear a previously saved field description in Data Reference and submit the edit. The editor restores the old text instead of preserving the requested empty description, so clearing differs from saving another nonempty value.

rootCause.explanation: The reference update path distinguishes untouched values from changed values but the form/API normalization loses an explicit empty text edit, so the old metadata survives.

logicalBugs.explanation: A model is a saved, table-like query that other questions can use as a data source; it can also have custom column labels, types and display settings. Restore an earlier model revision or change an upstream model’s returned columns, then compare the result table with More info > Overview. The table uses the restored/new fields, but Overview lists old names, an old count or removed columns instead of describing the data currently returned.

rootCause.explanation: Overview SidesheetCardWithFields derives fields from Lib.returnedColumns(question.query(),-1), not the newly executed dataset response. If a revert or upstream source change leaves the query metadata provider stale, the field list retains its previous columns despite updated result data.

reproductionPaths.explanation: A model is a reusable saved query with an Info > Overview list of its columns. Restore an earlier model revision after renaming or removing a column. The table restores the earlier names and columns, but Overview keeps the newer names or incomplete field list rather than describing the restored results.

Open model menu > Edit metadata. Select Title column, change Display name to Member Product Name, and Save changes.
Refresh and verify Member Product Name is shown.
Open More info > History. Click revert next to 'You created this.'
Compare the returned Overview field list with the underlying table column header.

logicalBugs.explanation: In Metabase, a model is a saved query used as a table-like data source, and a metric is a saved calculation such as a sum. Restoring one from Trash, or restoring an earlier query definition through Info → History, can leave the open editor and information panel inconsistent with the restored saved item. Depending on the path, editing still uses the Trash location, the source link is absent, the definition refers to the item itself, or an existing bookmark appears inactive. The data or restored item can be present while these controls still describe an earlier state; the affected restore workflow and visible discrepancy must match.

rootCause.explanation: Restore updates the entity record but leaves the query-builder card/original-card and collection/source metadata stale; editing, bookmarks and Overview continue to use the archived/self-referencing representation until reinitialization.

reproductionPaths.explanation: A metric is a saved calculation. A model is a reusable saved query. Restore an open model or metric from Trash, then use that same page without reloading. Renaming or converting it can show a permission error, and Duplicate can remain disabled despite valid inputs. Reloading makes those operations work; the problem follows the completed Restore rather than an actual lack of permission.

sourceBugs.name: Editing a restored model or metric from its open page fails because it still points at Trash

reproductionPaths.expected: After restoring from the trash banner, renaming, converting or duplicating the model or metric works without a reload.
reproductionPaths.actual: The open page still sends the Trash collection: renaming or 'Turn back to saved question' shows 'Sorry, you don't have permission to see that', and Duplicate stays disabled with valid inputs. Reloading fixes it.
reproSteps: Sign in as a member (maya@example.test). Create a model from Products, then a metric that counts it.
Move the model to the trash, open the metric and follow its source link. Confirm the model-in-trash banner.
Click Restore. After the trash banner disappears, rename the model and press Enter.
Observe the view is replaced by "Sorry, you don’t have permission to see that."

reproductionPaths.explanation: A model is a reusable saved query. Its Overview should identify the table supplying its data under Based on. Change its source from Products to People, save, then use History to restore the earlier Products revision. Products rows return, but Overview loses the Based on section instead of linking to Products. This path restores a revision, not an item from Trash.

sourceBugs.name: Restoring model query source loses Based on source link in Overview

reproductionPaths.expected: Overview identifies the restored Products source and links to it.
reproductionPaths.actual: Products data returns but Overview has no Based on section. Multimodal assertion checked the whole Overview and confirmed the source section is absent. Overview also retains 13 People fields rather than 8 Products fields (related stale-fields finding already filed).
reproSteps: Create Products notebook model with unique QA-MODEL name.
Edit query definition and change source table from Products to People; save changes and refresh.
Open Info > History; restore revision immediately preceding source change.
Inspect Info Overview after Products table results return.

reproductionPaths.explanation: A metric is a saved calculation. A model is a reusable saved query. Restore a saved model or metric from Trash and open its query-definition editor before refreshing the page. A model can list itself as its source instead of its original table; a metric can replace its original formula with its own name and omit a saved filter. Further editing can fail to save, while refresh restores the correct definition.

sourceBugs.name: Restored models and metrics open an incorrect self-referencing definition until refreshed

reproductionPaths.expected: Restore should retain the original source, formula and filters in the editor, and subsequent definition/metadata changes should be saveable.
reproductionPaths.actual: Metric43's post-Restore editor showed Formula 'Metrics QA Renamed' instead of Sum of Tax and omitted its saved Created At filter. Removing Default time dimension and saving showed Save failed; For a member-owned People model, Restore > Edit query definition showed its own model as Data instead of People.
reproSteps: Sign in, open /browse/metrics, open Revenue, and use its three-dot menu > Duplicate. Name the copy Metrics QA Restore Test and save in Our analytics.
Return to /browse/metrics and use the copied metric row's options > Move to trash.
Navigate to the copied metric's URL and click Restore.
Without refreshing or leaving that metric, open its three-dot menu > Edit metric definition.
Observe Formula contains the metric's own name instead of Sum of Total and the original date filter is missing.
Remove Default time dimension with its x control and click Save changes; observe Save failed. Refreshing the editor restores the correct formula.

Model variant: create a notebook model from Sample Database > People, trash it, reload its archived page, Restore, then immediately Edit query definition. Data incorrectly references the model itself, and metadata changes remain unsaveable until refresh.

reproductionPaths.explanation: A model is a reusable saved query. Bookmark a saved model, move it to Trash and restore it, then open it through the retained sidebar bookmark. The model toolbar shows the unfilled Bookmark icon as though it were not bookmarked, although that sidebar bookmark still exists.

sourceBugs.name: Restored bookmarked model opens with an inactive Bookmark control

reproductionPaths.expected: Opening a restored model from its sidebar bookmark should display an active (filled) bookmark icon.
reproductionPaths.actual: After restoring QA-MACT-A from Trash and opening it from the sidebar bookmark, the model toolbar displays an unfilled/outlined bookmark icon instead of an active filled bookmark icon.
reproSteps: As Harbor Admin, duplicate Orders + People to a fresh QA-MACT model in Examples.
Bookmark the duplicate and verify the filled bookmark icon.
Use model actions > Move to trash and confirm.
Open Trash; select Restore from that model's row actions.
Click the restored model's sidebar bookmark.

logicalBugs.explanation: A model is a saved, table-like query that other questions can use as a data source; it can also have custom column labels, types and display settings. Rename a calculated model output or replace its source so that the output columns change. Saved display names, descriptions and data-role choices can be discarded or attached to a different new expression, leaving labels that no longer describe the returned values instead of keeping each column’s customizations with the correct output.

rootCause.explanation: Model edit patches are keyed by focusedFieldName; Question.setResultMetadataDiff later applies each patch only through metadataDiff[column.name]. Renaming/replacing an output changes that identity, so saved per-column patches no longer attach to the renamed output or attach to a reused source name.

reproductionPaths.explanation: A column in a model (a reusable saved query) can have a custom display name, description and data role such as Currency. Rename a calculated output in the model’s query without changing the calculation. Saving discards those custom settings: the display name falls back to the new expression name, the description empties and the data role resets.

sourceBugs.name: Renaming a calculated model output discards its saved display name, description, and semantic type

reproductionPaths.expected: Renaming a calculated output in the query definition without changing its expression should retain its customized metadata, or explicitly warn that it will be discarded.
reproductionPaths.actual: After renaming the custom column in the query definition and saving, its custom Display name reverts to the new formula name ('QA Renamed Price'), the description is cleared, and the Column type resets from Currency to 'No semantic type'.
reproSteps: Create a model from Sample Database > Products and open Edit query definition.
Add custom column [Price] * 2 named QA Double Price and save.
In Edit metadata set that output's Display name to QA Calculated Cost, Description to Calculated output sentinel, twice product price., and Column type to Currency. Save and reopen the model.
Edit query definition, open QA Double Price and change only its name to QA Renamed Price. Update and Save changes.
Open Edit metadata and select QA Renamed Price.

reproductionPaths.explanation: A model is a reusable saved query. Save a model based on Orders, then change its source to People without editing column labels. The results contain people’s names but the name column keeps the unrelated User ID label from Orders, including after refresh. The error is an inherited label attached to the wrong new output.

sourceBugs.name: Changing an Orders model's source to People leaves the person-name column labeled User ID

reproductionPaths.expected: After switching to People, model columns should describe the People fields; its person-name field should not inherit the unrelated Orders User ID label.
reproductionPaths.actual: The saved People records display person names (Hudson Borer, Dominique Williamson, Lina Haney) under a column labeled User ID. This misleading inherited label remains after refresh; no column metadata edits were made.
reproSteps: From Models click plus, choose notebook editor, Sample Database and Orders.
Save a fresh uniquely named ML- model in Our analytics with default column metadata.
Open the model ellipsis menu and choose Edit query definition.
Replace Orders source with People and click Save changes.
Inspect the saved model and refresh.

logicalBugs.explanation: A model is a saved, table-like query that can show records as a list and open a single row in a detail view. An entity key is the column whose value identifies that record for search and navigation. Configure a column’s link URL or displayed link text to include another column’s value, such as an ID placeholder. Model tables can substitute that value correctly, but record details and administrative previews leave it empty even when the referenced value is visible in the same record; a placeholder for the current column can still work.

rootCause.explanation: Detail-view renderValue builds both visualization columns and clicked.data from only the current column/value. Cross-column template placeholders therefore lack the rest of the row, although table results format the same settings correctly. logicalBugs.explanation: Global search finds saved questions, dashboards, models and metrics, and can restrict results by content type, date or whether an item is in Trash. Use Creation date’s “Before” search filter with a selected calendar date. Results still include items created on that very day, rather than only earlier days; this is the exclusive-boundary error even when the item’s displayed timezone/day is otherwise consistent.

rootCause.explanation: The absolute ~date decoder returns the selected date as :end. Search requests date-string->range with inclusive-end? false, whose adjust-inclusive-range-if-needed adds one day to the end; search then compares timestamp-date < that advanced bound. This makes Before include the selected day. The conversion must distinguish an already-exclusive Before endpoint from an inclusive range endpoint.

logicalBugs.explanation: A model is a saved, table-like query that other questions can use as a data source; it can also have custom column labels, types and display settings. Pinned items occupy ordered positions at the top of a collection. Duplicating a pinned model places the copy in the first position and shifts the original rather than leaving the copy unpinned or preserving the original’s position; a later ordinary save can then describe that earlier shift as a new pin change in History.

rootCause.explanation: The copy flow builds a new card from the source Question while changing name, collection and description without clearing collection_position. create-card! accepts collection_position from input and explicitly reconciles existing collection positions before inserting the new card. Carrying the source’s pin into creation therefore places the duplicate there and moves the original. The later history pin diff reflects a real earlier shift, unlike a purely spurious history comparison.

Later, adding a row limit to the original model and saving records 'modified the query, edited the metadata and changed pin position.' (collection_position 1 -> 2).
